subject: Agriculture
title: Climate-Resilient Crops
description: A short lesson to help you apply Climate-Resilient Crops.

hook.text: Green Revolution varieties were bred for ideal conditions. Climate change creates anything but ideal.

buildup.text: Droughts, floods, and heat waves are increasing. Crops bred for stable weather fail when conditions shift.

discovery.text: Breeders are developing 'scuba rice' that survives two weeks underwater and drought-tolerant maize for Africa.

twist.text: Climate change moves faster than traditional breeding. New varieties may be obsolete before they're deployed.

climax.text: Gene editing tools like CRISPR could accelerate breeding from decades to years—if regulations allow it.

punchline.text: The next revolution must outrun the climate. Speed is everything.

quiz.question: What is 'scuba rice' designed to survive?
options: Two weeks of complete submersion underwater

details.summary: Climate-resilient crop varieties are bred to withstand drought, flooding, heat, and salinity—the stresses that climate change is intensifying. This topic covers how modern breeding and biotechnology are developing crops that can maintain yields as growing conditions become more extreme.
details.whyItMatters: Climate change threatens to reduce crop yields by 2-6% per decade in many regions. Developing varieties that tolerate extreme weather is essential for maintaining food security as temperatures rise and weather patterns become more volatile.
takeaways: Drought-tolerant maize varieties maintain yields 20-30% better than conventional hybrids
Submergence-tolerant rice (Sub1 rice) survives two weeks of complete flooding
Heat-tolerant wheat varieties are critical as growing seasons warm in South Asia

faq.question: How are breeders developing climate-resilient crop varieties?
faq.answer: Breeders screen thousands of traditional and wild varieties for stress tolerance genes. Marker-assisted selection identifies and combines multiple tolerance traits. The SUB1 gene from a traditional Indian rice variety was bred into modern varieties, creating rice that survives two weeks of flooding.

faq.question: Can crop breeding keep pace with the speed of climate change?
faq.answer: New tools like genomic selection and gene editing dramatically accelerate breeding. However, developing and deploying a new variety takes 8-15 years. Climate change may outpace breeding in some regions, requiring complementary adaptations like irrigation, changed planting dates, and crop switching.
